facts: Coordinates are written $(x, y)$ — **horizontal first**, then vertical.
$x$ is counted **right** from $0$; $y$ is counted **up** from $0$.
The point $(0, 0)$ is the **origin**, where the axes meet.
steps: Drop straight down from the point to read the $x$-axis value.
Look straight across to the $y$-axis to read the $y$ value.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$C$ is on the $y$-axis, so its horizontal coordinate is $0$. It is $3$ units up: $C=(0,3)$.

$D$ is on the $x$-axis, so its vertical coordinate is $0$. It is $5$ units across: $D=(5,0)$.

$O$ is the origin, where the axes meet: $O=(0,0)$.

$J=(3,1)$ and $K=(3,5)$ share horizontal coordinate $3$. They lie directly above one another on the same vertical grid line.

$K=(3,5)$ and $L=(6,5)$ share vertical coordinate $5$. They lie at the same height on the same horizontal grid line.

workedExamples.question_text: To reach $(7,3)$ from the origin, which direction do you move first, and how far? Which direction do you move next, and how far?
workedExamples.solution_text:
The first coordinate gives the horizontal movement: move $7$ units right.

The second coordinate gives the vertical movement: move $3$ units up.

foundation.question_text:
Write the coordinates of the point $O$ where the axes meet.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(0,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$O$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
The axes meet at the origin.
$O=(0,0)$

development.question_text:
Which two points have the same horizontal coordinate?
Give their coordinates. The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(2,1)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$J$};\fill(2,5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$K$};\fill(5,2)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$L$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
$J$ and $K$ lie on the same vertical grid line.
$J=(2,1)$ and $K=(2,5)$

development.question_text:
Which two points have the same vertical coordinate?
Give their coordinates. The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(1,4)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$M$};\fill(5,4)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$N$};\fill(4,1)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$P$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
$M$ and $N$ lie on the same horizontal grid line.
$M=(1,4)$ and $N=(5,4)$

development.question_text: To plot $(8,5)$, start at the origin and move $8$ units in which direction, then $5$ units in which direction?
development.solution_text: Move $8$ units right, then $5$ units up.

development.question_text:
Write the coordinates of the four labelled corners. The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\draw(1,2)--(5,2)--(5,5)--(1,5)--cycle;\foreach \x/\y/\l in {1/2/A,5/2/B,5/5/C,1/5/D}{\fill(\x,\y)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$\l$};}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

mastery.question_text:
Name two plotted points with the same horizontal coordinate and give their coordinates. What do you notice about their positions? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(7,7);\draw[->](0,0)--(7.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,7.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(4.5,2.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$A$};\fill(4.5,6.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$X$};\fill(1.5,6.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$B$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
mastery.solution_text:
$A=(4.5,2.5)$ and $X=(4.5,6.5)$ have the same horizontal coordinate, $4.5$.
They lie directly above one another on the same vertical line.

mastery.question_text:
The vertices of a rectangle are $P(2,1)$, $Q(6,1)$, $R(6,5)$ and $S$.
What are the coordinates of $S$?

A student records the coordinates of plotted point $P$ as $(6.5,2.5)$. Correct the error and explain the mistake. The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(7,7);\draw[->](0,0)--(7.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,7.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(2.5,6.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$P$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
mastery.solution_text:
Read $2.5$ along and $6.5$ up, so $P=(2.5,6.5)$.
The student swapped the horizontal and vertical coordinates.
